description.en-US: The fulfillment whose target moved. Every field on this record is immutable: it is an audit trail of something that already happened, and a row that could be edited afterwards would be evidence of nothing.

Where the goods were promised from before this change. Nullable, because a fulfillment whose reservation had expired holds no target at all, and recording a blank origin is more honest than inventing the one it used to have.
Where they are promised from now. Required: a change with no destination is not a change.

The reservation Inventory created at the new location. It is what ties a commercial decision to the physical hold that carried it out, so an operator investigating a shortfall can follow the goods rather than infer them. Opaque here and never interpreted.

Why the target moved, in business terms rather than technical ones. It is kept because the same movement means different things: a customer choosing another kiosk is a service event, while an operator moving stock away from a failing machine is an operational one, and a support agent reading the history needs to tell them apart. 'reservation_expired' marks the case where the old hold had already lapsed and a fresh one was taken rather than moved.

What sort of actor made the change, taken from the request's own authentication and never accepted from a caller. A workload is distinguishable from a person here precisely because 'the kiosk moved it' and 'a support agent moved it' are different answers to a customer asking why their order changed machine.

Which actor, when one was authenticated. Nullable, because a change made by a scheduled sweep has no principal to name, and recording an empty id is more honest than attributing it to whoever happened to trigger the run.
When it happened. Stamped by the server rather than accepted, so a history cannot be written out of order.
